conclusion: Positive final canonical NativeGrammar CPU integration proof for the explicit audited decision-schema subset on existing A28 runtime; exact requested facts emitted once in canonical order, every truth state remains possible. No arbitrary JSON Schema, GPU generation or latency claim.
limits: Current installed strict converter accepts examples violating not,uniqueItems,unknownformat,and pattern+maxLength; explicit policy rejection is essential.
A valid partial prefix truncated by token/time limits still fails complete JSON/schema validation; no repair or unconstrained fallback.
HF adapter calls .item() on the last token and moves a CPU bitmask to scores device every token; actual CUDA synchronization/copy/masking overhead and endpoint latency remain unmeasured.
Schemas with different frame alias count/fact sets may miss the bounded cache and incur cold compilation; startup warmup proves the normal16-frame schema only.
Constrained generation changes token selection; quality and recall must be compared with the frozen pipeline, and no speed-only sampling changes are justified.
Canonical ordering narrows permitted fact array permutations while preserving valid fact-ID-to-payload mappings; it does not force fact states or establish visual truth.
Full original schema and semantic postvalidation remain required for correct support, state consistency, candidate integrity and temporal/source binding.

Final CPU test used the actual public tokenizer and production NativeGrammar code with fake configuration/output-shape metadata, zero model instances; actual loaded model output embedding and CUDA execution require separate root-owned proofs.
